items.excerpt: Researchers affiliated with UTHealth Houston, competing as Novamab AI, placed among the top five teams in the international AIntibody Challenge, a blinded, prospective benchmark published in Nature Biotechnology. It is one of the first hard tests of whether AI-designed antibodies actually bind their targets in the lab.

Machine learning doesn't replace human intelligence, but it can outlast human endurance, which makes it a helpful tool for chemistry and materials discovery. New methods push self-driving labs closer to running materials discovery campaigns at real scale.

A Sungkyunkwan University team led by Prof. Sung Beom Cho built an LLM-based platform that generates new materials synthesis recipes, dramatically cutting the trial and error normally needed to get from a predicted compound to an actual sample.

Korean researchers built an AI active-learning framework for solid oxide electrolysis cells that reached its optimum with 17 high-fidelity simulations instead of 6,561 — about 60 hours of compute instead of nearly 23,000. It improved electrochemical performance 14% while cutting thermal gradients 80%.

HydroGym, an open reinforcement-learning proving ground from Washington, Michigan and German groups, trains and benchmarks AI controllers for fluid flow. Controllers trained on simple channel flows transferred to a wing simulation, cutting surface friction 38% and drag 11%.

Tohoku University's DigBat consolidates 3,816 experimental solid-state electrolytes and 27,645 conductivity entries into one AI-ready platform with built-in machine learning and an AI assistant, aimed at making solid-state battery research navigable rather than merely storable.

MIT researchers added a new component to AI models that design new materials, helping ensure the material will be stable and practical for real-world use. The CrysVCD approach could reduce the money and time spent screening out unusable generated designs.
Machine learning identified solvent formulations that produce highly homogeneous quantum dot films, a step toward brighter and more uniform QLED displays.

Classical tensor-network computation proved more accurate than a quantum annealer for some Ising spin glasses, another data point in the contest between learned classical solvers and quantum hardware.
Sidney Perkowitz surveys alternative, physics-inspired computing methods — neuromorphic spikes, spin-based devices and beyond — as a response to the energy cost of running today's AI models.
Google Research introduces GlucoFM, a foundation model trained on continuous glucose monitoring streams, extending the sensor-foundation-model idea from wearables into metabolic health research.
Google Research describes an AI tool that sifts wearable sensor data to prioritize candidate biomarkers, narrowing the search space researchers must validate in clinical studies.
Puzzles and games can reveal gaps in models' smarts. MIT Technology Review sets out seven tests that current AI systems still flub, and invites readers to try to outwit them.

LLMs need vastly more data than children to learn language. Cognitive scientists are reverse-engineering that data-efficiency gap in the hope of building far more efficient models — and learning something about developing minds.

Patents can only name humans as inventors — for now. When Insilico Medicine's generative platform proposed a pulmonary fibrosis drug, the press release credited the AI while the patent named five people.
The compute power exists. The models exist. What's missing is a system that coordinates them — GEN argues molecular discovery is moving from standalone models to orchestrated agents.

Whatever level of artificial intelligence is used in the lab, humans need to be in the lead throughout the process, a research team argues — a framework for keeping scientific intent from drifting to the machine.

An end-to-end, machine-learning-guided workflow from UChicago's Gagliardi lab carries a material from academic idea to manufacture-ready reality in a single discovery process, yielding two new zinc MOFs for separating methane from nitrogen.

Harvard SEAS engineers built Mobilio, a smartphone app that uses machine learning, built-in sensors and personalized audio beeps to give users with blindness or low vision continuous guidance and obstacle avoidance.

University of Essex researchers developed a new way to turn ordinary antibodies into AI-designed 'intrabodies' that work inside human cells, potentially opening new paths for treating Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Huntington's and motor neurone disease.
A new AI system lets robots plan their next move while they're still in motion — removing reaction delays and doubling task speeds without any extra computing overhead.

Berlin researchers combined proteomics with machine learning across plasma from more than 100 vasculitis patients, plus an independent Prague cohort, to identify seven blood proteins that reliably signal remission where CRP cannot.
